_comment: Generic classic-SharePoint (2010/2013/2016 on-premises) to SharePoint Online modern web part mapping rules. This file ships NO organisation-specific entries: viewNamePrefix, evidenceSources and every evidencePage are deliberately empty/neutral defaults. Point --mapping-rules at your own copy of this file to record project-specific evidence, or to add/override webPartTypes entries.

_meta.description: Rules-based mapping from classic on-premises SharePoint web part types to SharePoint Online modern equivalents.
_meta.notes: Grow a project-local copy of this file with each conversion run; the packaged default stays neutral.

architecturalRules.rule: CAML lives in the view, not the page
architecturalRules.detail: Classic: the CAML filter is embedded in the XsltListViewWebPart on the page. Modern SharePoint Online: CAML lives in a list view definition. A conversion must provision the target view first, then wire the modern List web part to that view.

architecturalRules.rule: Detect role before mapping: Primary / Child / Secondary
architecturalRules.detail: The first unconnected list view is Primary. A connected consumer is Child. Additional standalone views are Secondary. Role determines section placement and gap handling.

architecturalRules.rule: Capture relationship intent even for web parts that are not migrated
architecturalRules.detail: A connected consumer web part must record its parent/child relationship even though it is not migrated, so a later redesign has the evidence it needs.

architecturalRules.rule: Layout selection is data-driven, not always OneColumn
architecturalRules.detail: Layout is chosen by evaluating the rules in layout-rules.json against component counts, never hardcoded in script logic.
When evidence for a component is missing, emit a warning and a gap. Do not infer a mapping, and do not report an empty result as a success.

webPartTypes.notes: HTML content is preserved. SharePoint Online strips inline CSS on a/li/span elements; use div/table/heading elements for styling.
knownLimitations: Inline styles on <a>, <li> and <span> are stripped by SharePoint Online
Zero-width spaces should be stripped from the source HTML

webPartTypes.architecturalNote: CAML lives in the view definition, not in the page. Provision the view first, then reference it from the modern List web part.

variants.description: List view with no web part connection. Role: Primary or Secondary.
variants.spoComponent: modern List web part referencing a provisioned view
variants.viewProvisioning: Create a view on the target list using the CAML captured from the source, named with the configured view-name prefix, then reference it from the page web part.
variants.notes: Identity tokens such as <UserID Type='Integer'/> resolve in SharePoint Online list views, but the resolved user can differ between the source and target identity providers -- validate.
knownLimitations: CAML must be captured from rendered HTML or a views export, not from page XML
A view-provisioning step is required before the page is built
A configurable view-name prefix distinguishes pipeline-created views from pre-existing ones

variants.description: List view that sends the selected row's value to connected consumer web parts.
variants.spoComponent: modern List web part, standalone view only
variants.notes: Modern pages do not support the classic web part connection framework. The provider migrates as a standalone list web part: data displays, but row selection no longer filters child web parts.

enhancementHook.description: Client-side component with a row-click event plus filtered child queries

variants.description: List view that receives a filter from a connected provider. Role: Child. Relationship intent is captured for a future redesign.
variants.notes: Functional regression. Relationship metadata must still be captured so a later redesign has the evidence it needs.

enhancementHook.description: Client-side master/detail component, subject to the receiving tenant's data-classification rules

webPartTypes.spoComponent: modern Text web part containing an HTML table, or a Quick links web part
webPartTypes.notes: A modern section supports at most three columns; use a one-column section with a table for wider link grids.
knownLimitations: Click-to-expand grouping is not available in static HTML
Icon images require the source site assets to be migrated first

webPartTypes.notes: SharePoint Online blocks arbitrary script injection. Requires a reviewed and approved client-side component, or removal.

layoutMappings.notes: Default for web part pages that are primarily list-driven.
Content-only pages with no list views.
